# Citations

**[1]** "Understanding Success Criterion 1.4.3: Contrast (Minimum)." *W3C WAI*, WCAG 2.1.
<https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html>
Data extracted: AA requires 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text. Large text = 18pt (24px) or 14pt bold (~18.67px). 13px is normal text. Ratios must not be rounded (4.499:1 fails). Luminance formula: L = 0.2126R + 0.7152G + 0.0722B.

**[2]** "Understanding Success Criterion 1.4.11: Non-text Contrast." *W3C WAI*, WCAG 2.1.
<https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/non-text-contrast.html>
Data extracted: 3:1 minimum for UI components against adjacent colors. Borders must meet 3:1 if they are the only way to identify a control. State indicators must independently meet 3:1. Inactive components exempt.

Data extracted: Google Calendar created internal system for adapting colors to dark theme by "desaturating hues and defining brightness." Colors kept "emotional but legible" on charcoal gray backdrops. No specific hex values or desaturation percentages published.

Data extracted: Lc scale 0-106. Lc 90 preferred for body text (14px/400). Lc 75 minimum for body text columns (18px/400). Lc 60 minimum for content text. Lc 45 for headlines. Lc 30 absolute minimum non-body. Lc 15 for non-text elements.

**[15]** "Why APCA." *APCA Contrast Documentation*.
<https://git.apcacontrast.com/documentation/WhyAPCA.html>
Data extracted: WCAG 2.x "far overstates contrast for dark colors" — 4.5:1 can be functionally unreadable near black. WCAG 2.x can pass unreadable colors and fail readable ones. APCA uses perceptually uniform values independent of light/dark mode.

**[16]** "APCA Easy Introduction." *APCA Contrast Documentation*.

**[19]** "When to Use White Text on a Dark Background." *UX Movement*.

**[20]** "Designing for Colorblindness." *Smashing Magazine*, 2024-02.
<https://www.smashingmagazine.com/2024/02/designing-for-colorblindness/>
Data extracted: Avoid red+green+brown, pink+turquoise+grey, purple+blue, green+orange at identical lightness. Blue safest foundation hue. Use labels, icons, shapes alongside color. Never rely on color alone.

**[21]** "Inclusive Dark Mode: Designing Accessible Dark Themes." *Smashing Magazine*, 2025-04.
<https://www.smashingmagazine.com/2025/04/inclusive-dark-mode-designing-accessible-dark-themes/>
Data extracted: Interactive elements need >4.5:1 contrast. Avoid overly saturated colors in dark mode. Use dark gray (#121212) not pure black. Halation: "halo effects where text edges appear blurred or overly luminous" — mitigate with gray backgrounds and muted colors.
